prompt: Shopping is the favourite pastime of most of the young people. Why is this the case? Do you think they should be encouraged to do some other useful activities in their free time?
essay:
For most young people, browsing shops whether online or in person has become their favourite way to spend free time. Teenagers usually chase trends or they do not have much responsibility so their time gets wasted. In my view, they should be encouraged to spend some of that time on more productive activities.

Teenagers sometimes are influenced by their friends, for example, often a friend comments negatively on their clothes so they get upset and look for new trendy clothes to fit in. This can cost them time and money since trends change constantly. This becomes a cycle in which they are always buying something new to keep up. Social media plays a major role, as advertisements and influencers constantly show young people products they are told they need. As a result, many feel dissatisfied with what they already own and keep buying to close that gap.

Families in particular are well placed to guide teenagers towards activities with lasting value. For example, going to the gym or applying for a job that strengthens their professional profile. This can brighten their future because those who gain experience early tend to find better-paid work later, while those who do not may struggle. The same applies to health, which many people only start caring about when it is too late.

In conclusion, young people shop largely because of peer pressure and constant advertising. I believe families should encourage them towards activities such as work or exercise, which offer lasting benefits rather than temporary satisfaction.
